[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The diagnostic setting writes a Log Analytics workspace ID, but that ID comes from configuration locals rather than a reference to the managed workspace. When the workspace is created by this configuration, the setting can be attempted before the workspace exists; add an ordering dependency or reference the managed workspace ID.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The management-group diagnostic setting sends local.template_file_variables.log_analytics_workspace_resource_id as its workspaceId, but that value is assembled from configuration rather than the created workspace. When this module creates the workspace, the setting should wait for it to exist.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The diagnostic setting sends `workspaceId` from a generated configuration string rather than a reference to the workspace resource. When the module manages that workspace, it must exist before Azure can create the diagnostic setting; no dependency currently orders it ahead of `diag_settings`.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
azapi_resource.diag_settings sends management-group diagnostics to the Log Analytics workspace through workspaceId = local.template_file_variables.log_analytics_workspace_resource_id, which is just a string. Neither that reference nor its depends_on establishes an edge to azurerm_log_analytics_workspace.management, so the diagnostic settings can be created before the workspace exists and the apply will fail. It should depend on the workspace.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
azapi_resource.diag_settings creates diagnostic settings whose body sets `workspaceId = local.template_file_variables.log_analytics_workspace_resource_id`. That ID is built from resource names and never references the azurerm_log_analytics_workspace.management resource, so nothing forces the workspace to exist before the diagnostic settings are created. It should depend on the managed Log Analytics workspace (e.g. via a bare depends_on on azurerm_log_analytics_workspace.management).

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
azapi_resource.diag_settings uses local.template_file_variables.log_analytics_workspace_resource_id for its workspaceId, but does not depend on azurerm_log_analytics_workspace.management. The Log Analytics workspace must exist before the diagnostic setting can be created.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
azapi_resource.diag_settings writes diagnostic settings whose workspaceId (via local.template_file_variables.log_analytics_workspace_resource_id) is a string computed inside module.management_resources from coalesce() of plain values — no attribute reference reaches azurerm_log_analytics_workspace.management, so nothing guarantees the Log Analytics workspace exists before the diagnostic settings are created. If the workspace is created in the same apply, the azapi_resource call can fail or point at a non-existent workspace.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
:resource.azapi_resource.diag_settings creates Management Group diagnostic settings whose workspaceId (local.template_file_variables.log_analytics_workspace_resource_id) points at the Log Analytics workspace deployed by :resource.azurerm_log_analytics_workspace.management. That dependency only flows through locals/module outputs (module.management_resources is data-only), so no resource-level ordering exists; on a first apply the diagnostic settings could be created before the workspace exists and fail. Add an explicit depends_on on :resource.azurerm_log_analytics_workspace.management.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
azapi_resource.diag_settings writes the Log Analytics workspace resource ID (local.template_file_variables.log_analytics_workspace_resource_id) into its body, but this value is a computed string that creates no Terraform dependency on azurerm_log_analytics_workspace.management. When deploy_diagnostics_for_mg and deploy_management_resources are both enabled, the diagnostic settings can be created before the workspace exists, causing the azapi_resource call to fail against a non-existent workspace. azapi_resource.diag_settings should depend on azurerm_log_analytics_workspace.management (e.g. via depends_on) to guarantee the workspace is created first.

fix.expression: jsonencode({ properties = { logAnalyticsDestinationType = "null", logs = [{ category = "Administrative", enabled = true }, { category = "Policy", enabled = true }], workspaceId = try(values(azurerm_log_analytics_workspace.management)[0].id, local.template_file_variables.log_analytics_workspace_resource_id) } })

diagnostics.message:
[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
Policy-assignment role assignments can reference custom role definitions created by this configuration. The module has no dependency on the role-definition readiness delay, so it could attempt those assignments before Azure has replicated the definitions.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
Policy-assignment role assignments can use custom role definitions produced by this module. Their IDs are assembled from configuration strings, so the module has no inferred dependency on the role-definition readiness delay. It should wait for the same role-definition delay used before the other managed role assignments.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
azurerm_virtual_hub_routing_intent.virtual_wan sets routing_policy.next_hop to local.virtual_hub_azfw_resource_id[location], i.e. the ID of azurerm_firewall.virtual_wan, but that ID is a plain string. Its depends_on only covers the resource groups, virtual WAN and virtual hub, so Terraform may create the routing intent before the firewall exists; Azure requires the next-hop firewall to already exist.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
azurerm_virtual_hub_routing_intent.virtual_wan builds its routing_policy with `next_hop = local.virtual_hub_azfw_resource_id[location]`, i.e. the Virtual Hub Azure Firewall, but its depends_on only lists the resource groups, virtual WAN and virtual hub. The firewall (azurerm_firewall.virtual_wan) must exist before the routing intent can point at it, so add a bare depends_on on azurerm_firewall.virtual_wan.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
azurerm_virtual_hub_routing_intent.virtual_wan sets routing_policy.next_hop to the Virtual WAN Azure Firewall resource ID from a local value, but it does not depend on azurerm_firewall.virtual_wan. The Azure Firewall must exist before the routing intent is created, otherwise the routing intent creation can fail.
